implementation_state: Implemented. src/opencode/oauth.rs runs the Console device-code flow (start at POST /auth/device/code, poll POST /auth/device/token with grant_type device_code, refresh with refresh_token) and models the tokens (access, refresh, expiry, server, org). src/opencode/console.rs resolves the stored token, refreshing it in memory when it is expired or within 60s of expiry (single-flight per key_ref; the read-only secret store is not written back), and discovers the Console model catalog via GET {server}/api/config, dropping disabled models and mapping the capability/limit/cost fields like the published catalog. The pipeline (buffered, streaming and both rectifier retries) swaps an OpenCodeConsole provider's request key for the resolved access token and attaches the x-opencode-org-id billing header. ProviderKind::OpenCodeConsole carries the OpenAI dialect, the /inference/openai/v1 base and the locked OpenCodeCli shaping profile, and the desktop fetch-models command routes Console providers to the discovery path behind the new `opencode` feature. Verified by unit tests and fake-console integration tests (device-code login, refresh, /api/config discovery).
required_gates: Device-code start/poll/refresh succeeds and persists a usable token
Rotating access token refreshed with single-flight discipline on 401/expiry
x-opencode-org-id attached from the resolved org
unblock_condition: Not blocked; implemented and tested against a fake Console.

THE KINDS AND THE PROFILE WERE OFFERED BY A BUILD THAT CANNOT MAKE THEM WORK, AND THAT IS NOW SAID OUT LOUD. The two provider kinds and the `opencode_cli` client profile are configuration rather than code -- plain variants of `ProviderKind` and `ProviderClientProfile`, neither behind a `cfg` -- so they survive every build. The request shaping that makes OpenCode's gateway accept a request is not configuration, and the gateway checks a fixed fingerprint and rejects anything else. A build without the feature could therefore be *told* to use OpenCode and would have every request refused, and the desktop app is such a build: it ships the `ml` feature and not `opencode`. The snapshot now carries `opencode_available` and the providers page offers the kinds and the profile only where they work. **THE DECISION LEFT OPEN IS THE PRODUCT'S, NOT THE CODE'S**: enabling the `opencode` feature in the shipped desktop app would make the two providers work there, and nothing here prevents that. What is settled is that a build without the stack no longer offers a provider it cannot serve. The account subsystem is the precedent -- it is also opt-in, and it already had a flag and an honest empty state; the inconsistency was that the OpenCode kinds had neither. See E-155.
